Where margin disappears

Good people shouldn’t be the integration layer.

If your team spends the day copying, checking, chasing, or re-entering information, the workflow is asking for a better system.

01

Slow lead response

Calls, forms, and messages land in different places while the best opportunity goes to whoever responds first.

02

Dispatch handoffs

CSRs and dispatchers spend hours moving context between phones, inboxes, technicians, and customers.

03

Quotes that go quiet

Estimates rely on someone remembering the next follow-up instead of a system that knows what should happen.

04

Reporting by spreadsheet

Leaders wait for manually assembled numbers instead of seeing what changed, where, and why.

A practical path from friction to working system

Start small enough to prove. Build well enough to keep.

  1. 01

    Opportunity scan

    A focused 20-minute conversation about where work stalls, repeats, or depends on one person’s memory.

    20 min
  2. 02

    Workflow audit

    We map the current process, quantify the cost, and identify the smallest valuable automation worth building.

    7 days
  3. 03

    Implementation

    We connect the systems, build the workflow, test real edge cases, document it, and train the people who use it.

    30 days
  4. 04

    Ongoing improvement

    We monitor what was built, improve it with real usage, and tackle the next workflow only when the first is working.

    As needed
